issue_context.title: Documentation for "ansible-pull" does not make its top-level behaviour/purpose clear
issue_context.body:
### Summary

From the "Name" section of the man page, it says "pulls playbooks from a VCS repo and executes them for the local host". The "Description" section then starts "Used to pull a remote copy of ansible on each managed node [...]". It's really not clear what's remote and what's local.

I suspect "local" perhaps means "remote" in the context of "Name", because it's local to where the VCS repo was fetched (on the remote machine)? In any case, it seems confusing.

I'm still not entirely clear how it behaves, but I *think* I understand what it's for, and suggest replacing the "Name" section with something like "Configures remote hosts to regularly pull and execute an ansible script".

I would also suggest adding an example section to the ansible-pull documentation, which often clarifies things if a command's usage is not clear.

### Issue Type

Documentation Report

### Component Name

ansible-pull

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version
ansible [core 2.15.0]
  config file = None
  configured module search path = ['/Users/sgf/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /opt/homebrew/Cellar/ansible/8.0.0/libexec/lib/python3.11/site-packages/ansible
  ansible collection location = /Users/sgf/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
  executable location = /opt/homebrew/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.11.4 (main, Jun 15 2023, 07:52:47) [Clang 14.0.0 (clang-1400.0.29.202)] (/opt/homebrew/Cellar/ansible/8.0.0/libexec/bin/python3.11)
  jinja version = 3.1.2
  libyaml = True
```


### Configuration

```console
# if using a version older than ansible-core 2.12 you should omit the '-t all'
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all
CONFIG_FILE() = None
EDITOR(env: EDITOR) = emacs
PAGER(env: PAGER) = less
```


### OS / Environment

```
$ uname -a
Darwin wellington.local 21.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 21.6.0: Mon Aug 22 20:20:05 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8020.140.49~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T8101 arm64
```

### Additional Information

The ansible-pull documentation is not clear to a new user of Ansible (who is otherwise an experienced dev). Improving the docs will help new users get up to speed with this tool.

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow the Ansible Code of Conduct
comments:
Files identified in the description:
* [`lib/ansible/cli/pull.py`](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/cli/pull.py)

If these files are incorrect, please update the `component name` section of the description or use the `!component` bot command.

[click here for bot help](https://github.com/ansible/ansibullbot/blob/devel/ISSUE_HELP.md)
<!--- boilerplate: components_banner --->

"local" refers to the machine where ansible-pull is run on. ansible-pull fetches playbooks from a (remote) VCS repository and then runs ansible-playbook on the locally checked out copy of the VCS repository.

The text in "Description" (https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/cli/ansible-pull.html#description) on looks a bit like a very high-level description of an example, and not really like a description of what the tool really does. This should probably be rewritten from scratch (except the second paragraph, which can probably improved as well though).

@bcoca I'm not sure this should be closed, since only half of the issue is fixed. The short description is better now, but the main description (which is taken from the docstring: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/cli/pull.py#L36-L47) is still not great IMO.

review_comments:
While I agree with #81130 that the current formulation is bad, I don't think changing 'local' to 'remote' makes it any better. I think this would be slightly better than the current version in `devel`:
```suggestion
            desc="pulls playbooks from a VCS repo and executes them locally")
```
change to 'target' it is more agnostic and user can infer if local/remote depending on their context
